Supplementary conclusion: this case does not amount to "Triggered by a recent configuration change".

Our company's Level 3 response rules: for cross-site fiber optic cable interruptions that affect dedicated line users, the on-duty engineer must be notified immediately to go to the site for emergency repair. state: Line inspection data: At the S-700-9 site, the main fiber receiving power dropped from -12.4dBm to -24.8dBm, falling below the -20dBm tolerance. The network management triggered an optical path degradation alarm, and the optical time-domain reflection test found a 6.2dB attenuation step 1.1 km from the endpoint, suspected to be water ingress in the connector box. The protection switch was switched to the backup fiber within 80 milliseconds, with no service interruption. Only this single site was affected, and there were no similar alarms at surrounding stations. It has been included in the planned process and scheduled within this week, with no immediate personnel needed. Also: The oil engine test record dated 2026-09-16 is still missing one S-137-6 unit without signature. Supplementary conclusion: this case does not amount to "Cable break or severe optical path degradation".

Data shows that among the 38 cells linked under the S-852, S-454, S-837, and S-232 sites, PRB utilization remained at 92%~97% for 30 consecutive minutes, with congestion and packet discarded accounting for 8.4%, and user surface latency rising to 78ms. Preliminary judgment is that it is evening peak call overload, not a device alarm. An administrative duty staff member at a certain hospital called in the morning to inquire about the in-hospital room division coverage. A separate TK-20260926-1938 follow-up has been issued, which is unrelated to this topic. The expansion plan will be reviewed next week. Supplementary conclusion: this case does not amount to "Traffic overload causing congestion drops".
